body:
# Strata 0.2.4 (DSV4.1 engine 0.1.49) first run on RTX 5090 D v2 24 GB / 128 GB RAM: 7.9-10.2 tok/s decode, RAM store only ~50 GiB of ~60 GiB free

Hi,

First run of the new 0.2.4 DeepSeek package (engine 0.1.49, Windows CUDA13) on a bigger box than your test machines — the numbers sit inside your published range for 12 GB cards, but the RAM store did not grow anywhere near the RAM we have free, so we suspect we are leaving speed on the table. Setup itself was flawless: `--gguf-dir` picked up our already-downloaded ISTA shards + Engram, everything verified, model answered a sanity question correctly.

## System

| | |
|---|---|
| CPU / RAM | Intel 14700KF / 128 GB DDR5-4800 |
| GPU | RTX 5090 D v2 24 GB, Windows 10 |
| Model | ISTA-DASLab GSQ-RCO IQ2_XXS (257 GB set), files served via `--gguf-dir` from a local dir |
| Setup | `setup.py --family deepseek41 --model IST-DAS-2.00bpw --gguf-dir ... --dsv41-package strata-dsv41-0.1.49-windows-x86_64-cuda-cuda13.tar.gz --yes` |
| Engine defaults written by setup | `--max-context 8192 --eos 1 --dspark auto --dspark-conf 0.65; server 127.0.0.1:8080, gpu 0` |

## Numbers (r1: streaming chat, 256 completion tokens, same script as our other engine runs)

| seg | prompt tok | prefill | TTFT | decode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| r1-short | 70 | 5.5 tok/s | 12.7 s | **8.6 tok/s** |
| r1-long-2000 | 1277 | 52.4 tok/s | 24.4 s | **7.9 tok/s** |
| r1-long-8000 | 4943 | 240.1 tok/s | 20.6 s | **10.2 tok/s** |

Your published figures for the 2.00-bit set: RTX 5070 (12 GB, 64 GB RAM) ~4.7-5 tok/s, RTX 3060 (12 GB, 46 GB RAM) ~7.2 tok/s. We are a 24 GB card with double the RAM and land only slightly above the 3060 — plausible (expert supply, not GPU compute, is the bottleneck), but see the RAM-store point below.

## The observation: the RAM store stays small while the box has RAM to spare

While serving, total process memory sits around **62 GB** — the system has roughly 60 GB still free, and the CPU-side expert pool for this model is ~112 GB (13,035 experts). The README says the store "takes whatever RAM is free", but it stayed around 34-55 GB and the rest of the experts kept streaming from the NVMe.

For comparison, on the same machine the Xolotl engine's pinned-RAM arena is ~72 GiB with `STRATA_ARENA_SLICE_GIB=4`, and its 12 GiB of unpinned arena is exactly what it blames for lost decode.

## Questions

1. Is there a knob to make the RAM store fill all free RAM (or a fixed GiB target) on Windows — something like an arena/store size env or flag we missed? If the store held the full ~112 GB, the SSD tier would go to zero.
2. What decode should we expect from a 24 GB card + 128 GB RAM (store fully grown) on the 2.00-bit set — is 8.6-10.2 tok/s simply the expected band for this config, or a symptom of the small store?
3. `--dspark auto`: did it enable the drafter on this box, and where in the log do we confirm which way it decided?
4. TTFT is 12-24 s even on a 70-token prompt (first run after start). How much of that is cold Engram rows / first expert reads, and does it shrink once the store warms up?
5. Minor: setup wrote `--max-context 8192` by default. Any downside (besides KV memory) to setting 262144 for agent use?

Logs kept at `H:\Strata-0.2.4\setup-retry.log`. Happy to run any A/B — the card is free.
